questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: You use your arms to hold yourself up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees stay away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time?

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Practice on a quiet road first. The extra weight changes how your motorcycle handles, so you need to get used to it before riding in traffic.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. Follow all rules shown on these regulatory signs.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest chance of a conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts are most likely. Be extra alert when another vehicle could cross in front of you.

questions.question: How can you be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position your motorcycle where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around you to avoid hazards. Do not assume eye contact means a driver sees you.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or stress make you drowsy and may impair your riding. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you stay in your lane?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. This gives you more space to react to hazards.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger NOT to do before a ride?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Get on the motorcycle only after the engine is started.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far back as possible.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should mount after the engine starts. They should hold the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should stay quiet and still.

questions.question: What should you do when riding through a turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Front wheel wobbling or shaking can be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because of improper load, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, you should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line or sign. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before entering the cross traffic lane. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire provides power, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making mirrors hard to use.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is only a problem if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a violent crash and serious injury. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When this happens, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect riding if you drink alcohol with the medication.
Have the same effect on everyone.

questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (including prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs) have side effects that can impair your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal if you safely can. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is less dangerous than hitting another car.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be prepared to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others and make sure they understand your plans. Signal clearly and position yourself well. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Watch ahead and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: What may help if your drive chain slips?
questions.explanation: Tightening the chain may fix slippage. If tightening does not work, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Do not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one at a time. Do not brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When riding, the best protection for a rider is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to stay away from other vehicles. Leave plenty of space so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper safety gear is also important.

questions.question: After you mount your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check that the mirrors are clean.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes all work. Clean and adjust your mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open, not closed.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, all of the following are hazards, except:
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Also watch for wind gusts from the vehicle and objects that passengers might throw. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour on average?
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. The time needed to lower blood alcohol can vary. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What can you do to make your motorcycle more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take quick action if needed.
